thread:
maria-release: heads up — canary started at 10:05 UTC and deploybot triggered autosafety at ~10:12. metrics show p95 up ~80ms and error-rate bump to 0.9% on /v1/generate. not huge but noisy. thoughts?
lee-sre: can you paste the deploybot signal? was it p95 or error threshold that fired?
deploybot: DeployBot: Canary signal: latency_p95 = +78ms (threshold 60ms), error_rate = 0.9% (threshold 0.5%), duration = 6m. Auto-rollback = SUPPRESSED (human-in-loop required for ambiguous signals).
tom-ops: thanks — looks like both thresholds touched but neither sustained >10m. since deploybot suppressed auto-rollback, suggestion: keep canary running but reduce traffic slice to 5% and monitor 15m. can we also pin the older model version for a quick revert if needed?
sara-eng: re: pin — we can pin to v2.3.1 on the routing layer, that'd be an immediate fallback. pinging infra to stage the roll-back command.
maria-release: good. also want comms plan if we do unwind: short note in #customers-affected and update release notes with a rollback blurb. nina-cs can you stand by? @nina-cs
nina-cs: standing by, will draft a customer-facing blurb if we decide to roll back. prefer to avoid alarming wording: "temporary degradation — mitigation in progress".
lee-sre: quick triage: timeline wise, spike aligns with a kernel flag flip we enabled in the runtime patch (kv-cache change). rolling that back locally reproduces the bump in staging. suggests variant degradation rather than infra flake.
sara-eng: thanks lee — if it's the kv-cache flag, we can flip it off in prod nodes for canary subset. ops, do we want to do that vs full rollback? flipping flag is safer.
tom-ops: agree — plan A: flip kv-cache flag off for canary slice (5%) and watch 10m. Plan B: if no improvement, pin traffic back to v2.3.1 and execute manual unwind. who has authority to approve the pin?
maria-release: I'll approve the pin if plan A fails. go ahead with the flag flip now. @deploybot can you run the flag toggle for canary nodes? include command in thread.
deploybot: DeployBot: executing runtime flag toggle on canary nodes: `runtime.kvcache.enabled = false` for nodes tagged canary-6177. ETA ~30s. Logging action id: db8f3c.
sara-eng: done — flipping now. cc @lee-sre
lee-sre: metrics starting to trend down, p95 -> +20ms and error_rate -> 0.35% after ~90s. nice.
maria-release: great. hold for 15m to ensure stability. reminder: release notes update in case we revert should be ready (nina draft).
nina-cs: drafted: "We observed a brief increase in latency and error rate for a subset of requests after today's deployment. Our engineers identified a runtime flag interaction and mitigated the issue; no customer data was affected. We'll post a follow-up if any further actions are needed." will post to #customers-affected if we proceed with pin or rollback.
tom-ops: heads up for ops rotation: if we need to pin, procedure is: 1) notify legal & support, 2) set routing pin to v2.3.1 with `redwood route pin --model gen-api --version v2.3.1`, 3) monitor & open rollback ticket, 4) update release notes. try to limit blast radius.
sara-eng: adding runbook note: add a canary tag annotation so dedicated customers don't get spilled traffic. `ops:annotation=canary-rollback-6177`.
maria-release: sounds good. leaving this thread open for the 15m watch. if p95 stays <= +25ms and error_rate <0.5% for 15m we close and log as "false positive/no action". if it regresses we escalate to pin + customer comms.
lee-sre: agree. if we escalate, I'll lead the rollback execution and post postmortem notes.
maria-release: thanks all, nice quick teamwork :thumbsup:
